headline: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment

members.title: Helen Haines live updates: Alleged attacker Brendan Nugent to face court in Wangaratta this morning
members.lead: Follow the day’s news live. ‘Deeply appalled’: politicians condemn alleged attack after Helen Haines critically injured Helen Haines, the principled MP respected across parliament The sister of murdered UK MP Jo Cox has said the attack on MP Dr Helen Haines could be a moment for Australia to “find common ground” and change the way politics is practised in this country. Cox was killed in 2016, shot and stabbed by a far-right extremist outside a library as she prepared to meet with constituents. That was something my sister was brilliant at and I would imagine it’s something Helen is good at. I am devastated for Helen and for her family, her friends, her colleagues, her staff, that I am probably one of the few people, I suppose, that can understand a little bit of what they’re going through. I find it really frustrating that we’re having the same conversation and every time something so horrific happens. Things don’t happen in a vacuum and horrendous attacks and incidents like this don’t happen in isolation. They are part of a wider culture around politics and society [and] we all have a role to play in that. Continue reading...

members.title: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment
members.lead: AFP commissioner says MPs are generally concerned about growing volume of abuse and intimidation Follow our live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians. But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack.
